extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers writing mathematical/technical academic papers (operations research, EE, applied math)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical style and structure guidelines for writing clear, readable academic papers that contain mathematical notation, theorems, proofs, figures, and tables; aimed at graduate students and researchers in applied math, EE, and operations research. Emphasizes sentence- and section-level clarity, notation discipline, theorem/proof presentation, figure/table best practices, introduction structure, and revision habits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Break long sentences into multiple sentences
rubrics_metrics.description: Break long sentences into multiple sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mathematical sentence with three subclauses is unparsable. Prefer splitting complex clauses so each sentence is easy to parse.

rubrics_metrics.name: One idea per sentence
rubrics_metrics.description: One idea per sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not combine a definition, claim, and proof step in the same sentence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer short sentences over long
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer short sentences over long.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short sentences improve readability in mathematical writing; avoid needless syntactic complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use active voice when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Use active voice when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active voice is generally clearer and more direct than passive constructions in exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid nominalizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid nominalizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use verbs instead of nominalized forms — e.g., 'We prove convergence' is better than 'A proof of convergence is provided.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep sections to one theme
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep sections to one theme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a section grows beyond three pages, split it; sections should be cohesive and focused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each section has a topic sentence
rubrics_metrics.description: Each section has a topic sentence that previews its contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin sections with a sentence that tells the reader what to expect in that section.

rubrics_metrics.name: End sections with a transition sentence
rubrics_metrics.description: End sections with a transition sentence to the next.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Close sections by signaling how material connects to what follows to keep the narrative flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sub-sections aggressively
rubrics_metrics.description: Use sub-sections aggressively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize material into ~two-page chunks so readers can resume easily after interruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number sections so cross-references stay valid
rubrics_metrics.description: Number sections so cross-references stay valid under revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use explicit numbering for sections/subsections to avoid broken references when rearranging content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimal notation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't introduce a symbol you use only once; keep notation lean to reduce cognitive load.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mnemonic letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Mnemonic letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose letters that suggest their meaning (e.g., G for graph, A for matrix) to aid reader memory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent typography
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent typography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt consistent typographic conventions (example: matrices uppercase bold; vectors lowercase bold; scalars italic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid stacked subscripts and superscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid stacked subscripts and superscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple stacking like A_i^{(j)} is acceptable; deeply nested indices such as A_{i_1}^{j_1^{k}} are confusing and should be avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't reuse a letter for two different objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't reuse a letter for two different objects in the same paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reusing symbols for different meanings in one manuscript confuses the reader; keep symbol usage unique within context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define every symbol on first use
rubrics_metrics.description: Define every symbol on first use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even 'obvious' symbols should be defined when first introduced to avoid ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: State a theorem in full English before formal statement
rubrics_metrics.description: State a theorem in full English before stating it formally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give an informal English description of the claim to provide intuition before the formal mathematical statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish theorem-like results by significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish theorems, propositions, lemmas, corollaries by significance and place in the argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use different labels to communicate the role and importance of results within the paper's logical structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place a proof immediately after the theorem
rubrics_metrics.description: A proof comes immediately after the theorem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid postponing proofs since delayed proofs interrupt reader focus and the logical flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a roadmap for long proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Long proofs need a roadmap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preface long proofs with a brief (e.g., three-line) preview of the global strategy to help readers follow the structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Every figure needs a self-contained caption
rubrics_metrics.description: Every figure needs a self-contained caption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captions should explain what the figure shows so the figure can be understood without referring back to the main text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label axes with units
rubrics_metrics.description: Axes labeled with units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include units on plot axes to make data interpretation unambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place legends inside the plot when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Legends inside the plot, not in the caption when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Putting legends within the plot keeps the visual association immediate; use caption for supplementary explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables: consistent placement of totals
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables: row totals at the bottom, column totals at the right (consistency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a consistent layout for tables so readers learn where to find summary information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction — first paragraph: problem and importance
rubrics_metrics.description: First paragraph: the problem and why it matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open by stating the problem and motivating its significance to engage a broad audience quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction — second paragraph: prior work in one paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Second paragraph: prior work in one paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize prior relevant literature concisely in a single paragraph to orient the reader without overloading detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction — third paragraph: contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Third paragraph: contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state what the paper contributes relative to prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction — fourth paragraph: paper outline
rubrics_metrics.description: Fourth paragraph: paper outline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a brief map of the paper's structure so readers know where to find details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sleep on the draft
rubrics_metrics.description: Sleep on the draft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let drafts rest before revision to return with fresh perspective and spot weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read aloud
rubrics_metrics.description: Read aloud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reading text aloud helps catch awkward phrasing and parsing problems that silent reading may miss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show to a colleague not in the field
rubrics_metrics.description: Show to a colleague who is not in the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-specialist readers reveal assumptions and clarity issues; use their feedback to improve exposition for a broader audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cut 10 percent of every section in the second pass
rubrics_metrics.description: Cut 10 percent of every section in the second pass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be ruthless in trimming excess material on revision passes to tighten exposition and improve readability.
